action: No action needed; for awareness. Gatwick's email to drivers, as relayed by Cedar News, says drop-off can be paid by other methods on its website.
date_note: Cedar News (24 November) reports the airport's email to drivers as sent on Tuesday 24 November; the page gives no earlier day for the unauthorised access.
exec: Gatwick says personal and, in some cases, partial card details of AutoPay drop-off users may have been exposed through a third-party system.
geo_basis: Gatwick Airport, West Sussex, UK; airport location, not the location of the third-party system
impact: According to Cedar News's account of the airport's email, names, contact details, AutoPay login information and vehicle registrations may have been exposed, and in some cases card brand, last four digits and expiry date.
plain: Gatwick Airport says it switched off its AutoPay drop-off payment service after someone got into a third-party system. It warns some personal details, and in some cases partial card details, may have been exposed.
summary: Cedar News reports that Gatwick Airport disabled its AutoPay drop-off payment service after unauthorised access to a third-party system. In an email to drivers, the airport said personal information may have been exposed and partial card details may have been affected in some cases. Cedar News says external specialists are investigating and the UK Information Commissioner's Office has been notified; no count of people is given.
title: Gatwick Airport disables AutoPay after unauthorised access to a third-party system, warns of possible data exposure

validation.note: Only Cedar News read; it relays an email from Gatwick to drivers. Gatwick's own page and the email were not found; a second publisher was not found in a search.

review.note: Compared title, date, exposed data, ICO, no count, status against Cedar News
